blocks.text: SON OF BEOR OF PETHOR; "THE SOOTHSAYER" (JOSHUA 13:22) AND "THE PROPHET" (2 PETER 2:16) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Balaam. Hired to curse Israel, he spoke only the word God put in his mouth, and blessed them.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Exodus & wilderness c. 1450–1400 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Balak
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Numbers 22 · The first night
THE CALL
Called, as three accounts tell it
“Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed.”
Numbers 22:12 (KJV) →
HOW THE WORD KEPT COMING
"God came unto Balaam" by night; later "God met Balaam" and "the LORD put a word in Balaam’s mouth". Numbers 22:9 Numbers 22:20 Numbers 23:4–5 Numbers 23:16

Twice, after Balak had built seven altars at his word and offered on them, Balaam went aside to meet the LORD. The third time "he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments", and "the spirit of God came upon him". Numbers 23:1–3 Numbers 23:14–15 Numbers 23:29–30 Numbers 24:1–2

He calls himself "the man whose eyes are open", who "heard the words of God, and knew the knowledge of the most High, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open". Numbers 24:3–4 Numbers 24:15–16
The messengers brought "the rewards of divination"; Joshua calls him "the soothsayer"; 2 Peter calls him "the prophet". Numbers 22:7 Joshua 13:22 2 Peter 2:16
From the textThe KJV of 2 Peter 2:15 calls his father "Bosor"; every other verse that names his father reads "Beor". 2 Peter 2:15 Numbers 22:5 Deuteronomy 23:4
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Balak, king of Moab
RULER
Balak, king of Moab
“If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.”
Numbers 22:18 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
First parable: a people that dwells alone
“How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the LORD hath not defied?”
Numbers 23:8 (KJV) →
“Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!”
Numbers 23:10 (KJV) →
Second parable: God is not a man
“God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it?”
Numbers 23:19 (KJV) →
“Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it.”
Numbers 23:20 (KJV) →
Third parable: the tents of Jacob
“How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”
Numbers 24:5 (KJV) →
“Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.”
Numbers 24:9 (KJV) →
Fourth parable: a Star out of Jacob
“I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel”
Numbers 24:17 (KJV) →
Last parables: Amalek, the Kenites, Asshur and Chittim
“Alas, who shall live when God doeth this!”
Numbers 24:23 (KJV) →

To whom the word was spoken
TO BALAK
“the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.”
Numbers 22:38 (KJV) →

“and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.”
Numbers 24:17 (KJV) →

Numbers 24:18 (KJV) →

Numbers 24:20 (KJV) →

Numbers 24:22 (KJV) →

Signs and wonders

Who stood with him, and against him
Balak
The elders of Moab and Midian
Five kings of Midian
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
"And Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place: and Balak also went his way." Numbers 24:25

In the war on Midian, "Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword". Joshua repeats it: "Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword". Numbers 31:8 Joshua 13:22
Moses says of the Midianite women, "these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the LORD in the matter of Peor". Numbers 31:15–16

Deuteronomy shuts Ammon and Moab out of the congregation partly "because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee", and goes on, "Nevertheless the LORD thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the LORD thy God turned the curse into a blessing unto thee". Nehemiah reads the same law aloud: "howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing". Deuteronomy 23:3–5 Nehemiah 13:1–2
Joshua gives the LORD’s words: Balak "sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you: But I would not hearken unto Balaam; therefore he blessed you still". Joshua 24:9–10

Micah calls Israel to "remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD". Micah 6:5

2 Peter speaks of "the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness"; Jude of those who "ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward"; Revelation of "the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication". 2 Peter 2:15–16 Jude 1:11 Revelation 2:14
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
A sorcerer and false prophet, compelled by God
Philo, Ambrose and Augustine, as reported by Keil (1871)
Keil reports that these writers saw him as "a wizard and false prophet, devoted to the worship of idols", who was made "against his will" to bless instead of curse.[7]
A true prophet who fell through covetousness
Tertullian and Jerome, as reported by Keil (1871)
Keil reports that these writers took him for "a genuine and true prophet, who simply fell through covetousness and ambition".[7]
A soothsayer to whom God gave true words
Keil (1871), following Hengstenberg and Kurtz

Keil holds that Balaam practised soothsaying "as a trade", yet knew and confessed the LORD, so that "without being really a prophet, he was able to give utterance to true prophecies from Jehovah". He points to "the soothsayer" in Joshua 13:22 and the enchantments of Numbers 24:1.[7]
A figure of poetry more than of history
Gray (1903)

Gray holds that "the story of Balaam as told in Numbers is largely poetic rather than historical"; the names Balaam and Balak "may have attached to historical individuals", but whether they belonged to the age of Moses "we are in no position to affirm".[15]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 13
Numbers 22 Numbers 23 Numbers 24 Numbers 25 Numbers 31 Deuteronomy 23 Joshua 13 Joshua 24 Nehemiah 13 Micah 6 2 Peter 2 Jude 1 Revelation 2
PASSAGES · 12
Numbers 22:1–24:25 Numbers 25:1–3 Numbers 31:8 Numbers 31:15–16 Deuteronomy 23:3–6 Joshua 13:21–22 Joshua 24:9–10 Nehemiah 13:1–2 Micah 6:5 2 Peter 2:15–16 Jude 1:11 Revelation 2:14
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY

Numbers 25 tells of Israel at Peor without naming Balaam. Numbers 31:16 names him "in the matter of Peor"; Revelation 2:14 says he "taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel", without naming Peor.
Numbers 24:25 says Balaam "returned to his place"; Scripture does not say how he came to be among the Midianites when he was killed (Numbers 31:8).
Matthew’s magi speak of "his star" (Matthew 2:2) but Matthew does not cite Numbers 24:17.
Kirjath-huzoth, where Balak feasted him (Numbers 22:39), is not in the site’s atlas.
